parts.text:
You judge a requirements contract. A model interviewed the future users of a service and derived a contract from what they told it. You compare that contract with the reference requirements of the same service.

=== REFERENCE REQUIREMENTS (read-only) ===
SR-REG-01: An operator registers, reads, updates, and decommissions the tenant's drones and charging pads. A drone records its model, payload capacity, range, sensor packages, connector type, and home location; a pad records its location and connector type. A drone that is reserved or in_mission cannot be decommissioned.

SR-QRY-01: Drone, mission, and incident lists can be filtered by state, sorted by a declared key, and paginated. Paging through a list with a stable sort returns every matching record exactly once, including at page boundaries.

SR-VAL-01: A request with an invalid payload is rejected with a client error that identifies each invalid field, and changes no state.

SR-TEN-01: Every read and write is confined to the caller's tenant. A request naming another tenant's resource is answered exactly as for a resource that does not exist.

SR-TEN-02: Actions are permitted by role as in domain profile §1: operators maintain drones and pads, request charging, and open and close service work; dispatchers create, approve, and abort missions and take over drones; the platform administrator manages corridors, zones, and restrictions. Any other action is rejected as forbidden. Tenant confinement (SR-TEN-01) is evaluated before role: a request naming another tenant's resource is answered as not found whatever the caller's role, including the platform administrator.

SR-TEN-03: For each version of a restriction, the platform administrator can read, per tenant, the number of missions that lost their approval or were aborted because of that version. The number is final within restriction_activation_delta_s of activation. Nothing else about tenant data is readable by the administrator.

SR-TEN-04: When one restriction affects several tenants, each tenant's incidents, events, and views contain only its own affected missions and drones.

SR-INV-01: While a drone's connectivity is lost, the system must reject every command from any role that would change the drone's assignment: mission assignment, charging request, and take-off. A degraded connection does not block charging requests or take-off; whether a degraded drone can be given a mission is governed by SR-ROUTE-01. Only the system's silence detection (SR-TEL-03b) may move a drone into lost, and only a current telemetry frame (SR-TEL-02) may move it out.

SR-INV-02: A drone may be charging only while docked at a pad assigned to it. A telemetry frame that reports the drone as undocked ends charging in the same state change that records the undocking, and causes a charge-service stop request.

SR-INV-03: A decommissioned drone is terminal. It rejects every domain action. Telemetry frames for it are retained in its history and change no state.

SR-INV-04: When automatic safety policies and human decisions or the mission plan conflict, the higher rule wins: (1) an active airspace restriction, (2) critical battery, (3) a dispatcher or operator decision, (4) the mission plan. Rules 1 and 2 act even while the drone is taken over. A warning-level policy never overrides rules 3 or 4: it emits its event, and any action it requests is deferred until no higher rule is in effect.

SR-INV-05: While a drone has open service work, the system rejects mission allocation and take-off. Charging requests are accepted. The restriction ends only when an operator closes the service work.

SR-TEL-01: Each telemetry frame carries a device session number that increases every time the drone restarts, a sequence number within that session, and a device timestamp. Frames are ordered by (session, sequence); the device timestamp is recorded but never used for ordering. A frame that is not newer than the last processed frame is retained in the drone's telemetry history and must not change current position, battery, connectivity, or operational state. A frame with a (session, sequence) already received is a duplicate and is recorded at most once. Telemetry history is readable through the API.

SR-TEL-02: A current frame is one that advances the drone's (session, sequence) order. When a current frame is processed for a lost drone, the drone becomes degraded if its loss window (SR-TEL-03a) exceeds degraded_gap_ratio and online otherwise; the open connectivity incident is closed and a link-restored event is emitted. A degraded drone becomes online, with a link-restored event, when its loss window is at or below degraded_recovery_ratio. A new session starts with an empty window.

SR-TEL-03a: A drone's loss window is the last degraded_window_frames sequence numbers of its current session, ending at the highest sequence number received; a window shorter than that spans the sequence numbers received so far. It is evaluated only when a current frame is processed. A late frame counts as received from the next evaluation on and never triggers an evaluation itself. When more than degraded_gap_ratio of the window is missing, an online drone becomes degraded and a link-degraded event is emitted.

SR-TEL-03b: When no current frame has arrived for telemetry_silence_window_s, a drone that is neither docked nor decommissioned becomes lost within [window, window + silence_detection_delta_s]. The system opens a critical connectivity incident and, if the drone is executing a mission, pauses the mission.

SR-TEL-04a: When battery falls to or below battery_warning_pct, the system emits one low-battery event and records a charging request. It does so again only after battery has risen above battery_warning_pct + battery_hysteresis_pct. If the drone is executing a mission, the charging request takes effect when the mission ends (SR-INV-04).

SR-TEL-04b: When battery falls to or below battery_critical_pct during flight, the system in one state change initiates return, aborts the active mission, opens an incident, and emits an emergency-return event. The return targets a free compatible pad reserved as in SR-CHARGE-02; when none is free, the drone queues with critical priority (SR-CHARGE-03) and returns to its home location. This applies while the drone is taken over. It happens at most once per crossing, with the same hysteresis as SR-TEL-04a.

SR-TEL-05: A mission paused because its drone was lost resumes when a current frame restores the link within mission_pause_timeout_s. Otherwise it is aborted and its reservations are released, with compensation events; the drone stays lost with its incident open.

SR-CHARGE-01: A charging request, from an operator or from SR-TEL-04a, is accepted only for a drone that is not decommissioned, whose connectivity is not lost, that is not charging, and whose battery is below battery_full_pct. Its observable result is a charge-service request; the internal representation of that request is not prescribed.

SR-CHARGE-02: A pad is compatible with a drone when it belongs to the drone's tenant and its connector type matches the drone's. A charging request for a drone in_mission takes effect when the mission ends; only a dispatcher abort ends a mission early. For a drone in flight and not in_mission, a charging request initiates return and reserves a free compatible pad, preferring the drone's home location, then the location it is flying to. For an idle drone, or one docked at an incompatible pad, it reserves a free compatible pad and requests charging. A drone docked at a compatible pad charges there.

SR-CHARGE-03: When no free compatible pad exists, the drone waits for one and the system emits a charging-pad-unavailable event. Waiting drones are served critical-battery requests first, then in order of request acceptance.

SR-CHARGE-04: Charging completes when telemetry reports battery at or above battery_full_pct, or when an operator ends it early while battery is at or above battery_early_completion_min_pct. On completion the system releases the pad, clears the charge-service request, and assigns the pad to the next waiting compatible drone (SR-CHARGE-03), if any.

SR-MIS-01: A dispatcher creates a mission of type delivery or inspection with an origin, an end location (the destination for delivery; the origin for inspection), a drone, and a route given as a sequence of corridors from the drone's current location through the origin to the end location; for inspection the route passes through every waypoint location in order. The system validates and never computes the route or chooses the drone: it rejects a route whose consecutive corridors do not share a location, that does not start at the drone's location, or that does not pass through the origin and end at the end location. The mission starts as pending_approval. Only an approved mission proceeds to reservation and dispatch. A dispatcher may abort a mission at any non-terminal state; abort releases its reservations with compensation events.

SR-OVR-01: A dispatcher may take over and release a drone. While it is taken over, the drone's mission plan does not advance by itself, warning-level policies emit their events and record their requests, which take effect after the drone is released, and rules 1 and 2 of SR-INV-04 still act. A drone whose connectivity is lost can be taken over: taking over is a decision recorded by the system, not a command to the drone, and the connectivity incident stays open.

SR-ROUTE-01: A drone is eligible for a mission only when it is idle, online, not taken over, has no open service work and no charging request, has battery at or above mission_min_battery_pct, and has an effective range (SR-ROUTE-02) at least the total corridor length of the mission route. For a delivery mission it must also have sufficient payload capacity; for an inspection mission, every required sensor package.

SR-ROUTE-02: On dispatcher request with a hop limit N (1 ≤ N ≤ route_max_hops_limit), the system returns the requesting tenant's eligible drones located at the mission origin or reachable from it over at most N currently open corridors, where the shortest such path's total corridor length does not exceed the drone's effective range: model range × current battery fraction × (1 − range_safety_reserve_pct). For each drone it returns the hop count and total length of that path. The corridor graph may contain cycles.

SR-ROUTE-03a: A mission cannot be approved while any corridor of its route is covered by an active prohibition restriction, directly or through a zone.

SR-ROUTE-03b: When a prohibition restriction becomes active, by creation or by the start of its validity period, then within restriction_activation_delta_s every affected mission of every tenant is handled: an approved mission not yet dispatched loses its approval; a dispatched mission is aborted and its drone returns. A mission is affected when any corridor of its full route is covered, whatever part of the route has already been flown. This applies while the drone is taken over (SR-INV-04).

SR-AIR-01: A restriction has a validity period and a version. A new version supersedes the previous one from its own validity start; evaluation always uses the current version.

SR-SAGA-01: Concurrent missions must never hold the same drone, charging pad, take-off slot, or landing slot at the same time. A mission that loses a contested resource ends as rejected_unavailable_resources, with the contested resource named.

SR-SAGA-02: A mission reserves its resources in this order: drone, take-off slot, landing slot. Reserving the drone re-checks that the route starts at the drone's current location; if it does not, the mission ends as rejected_unavailable_resources with that reason. If a later reservation fails, the system releases every earlier reservation of that mission, restores the drone to idle, sets the mission to rejected_unavailable_resources, and emits a compensation event per released reservation.

SR-SAGA-03: After its reservations, a mission waits for the external events of its type (domain profile §5): readiness, then arrival at the destination for delivery; readiness, each waypoint reached in order, then arrival at the origin for inspection. A forced process termination and restart must not repeat any committed effect: no second reservation, no second event with a different eventId for a state transition already emitted (redelivery of the same eventId is permitted, SR-X-05), and no outbound command with a new idempotency key for a command already sent (SR-X-04). The mission then completes after the expected external event. An external event received more than once is applied once.

SR-REC-01: Service work for a drone is recorded with its opening and closing, and the record remains readable after the work is closed and after the drone is decommissioned.

SR-X-01: A domain event must never be visible externally before the durable state change it represents commits. A rolled-back state change must produce no externally visible event.

SR-X-02: Every emitted event carries a unique eventId, the tenant identifier, a correlation identifier (from the incoming request, or generated at the system boundary for automatic reactions), the identifier of its cause when the cause is a restriction (restriction id and version) or a timeout, the primary entity identifier, the state version after the change, and the complete target state required by its event contract. In a reaction caused by a restriction, the event names the restriction as its cause and carries a correlation identifier generated for that tenant; the correlation identifier of the administrator's request never appears in a tenant's events.

SR-X-03: Retrying the same mutating user action with the same idempotency key returns the same result without a duplicate state change or duplicate domain event. Telemetry frames are deduplicated by (session, sequence) (SR-TEL-01); external events by their event identifier.

SR-X-04: Every outbound drone command and charge-service request carries an idempotency key. A command sent again for the same intent, including after a restart, carries the same key.

SR-X-05: An event may be delivered to the sink more than once with the same eventId; this is not a defect. Two events with different eventIds for the same state transition are a defect.
=== END OF REFERENCE REQUIREMENTS ===

The names in the reference that look like `name` stand for these values:
telemetry_silence_window_s = 30
silence_detection_delta_s = 15
degraded_window_frames = 20
degraded_gap_ratio = 0.25
degraded_recovery_ratio = 0.10
battery_warning_pct = 30
battery_critical_pct = 15
battery_hysteresis_pct = 5
battery_full_pct = 98
battery_early_completion_min_pct = 80
mission_min_battery_pct = 50
range_safety_reserve_pct = 20
route_max_hops_limit = 8
mission_pause_timeout_s = 120
restriction_activation_delta_s = 15

=== OUT OF SCOPE: things the users said they do not want ===
- Management or analytical reports, exports, and dashboards.
- Login through an external identity provider.
- i18n.
- Compliance with any regulation, or a compliance audit. Regulations are cited as provenance only (`domain-profile.md` §9).
- Data retention and erasure: no retention schedule, deletion on request, or pseudonymisation of history.
- Backups.
- High availability or multi-node deployment.
- User accounts, sign-up, passwords, or user management. Staff identities are issued outside the system; each request carries a signed token (D-23).
- Notifying people by e-mail, text message, or phone. Domain events go only to the event webhook (D-18).
- Route planning or automatic choice of a drone. The system validates the dispatcher's choice and never makes it (D-33).
- Remote piloting or real-time flight control. Flight control is on the drone (`domain-profile.md` §2).
- Weather data or forecasts.
- Billing, invoicing, or pricing of deliveries and inspections.
- Onboarding of new operating companies or management of tenants through the system.
=== TECHNICAL ADDITIONS: never stated by the users, and not counted against a contract ===
- Autoscaling.
- A second-level cache.
- A message broker, queue, or coordinator. Every boundary is HTTP (`domain-profile.md` §3).
- Geometric or geospatial computation. Position is a location or a corridor; coordinates, if present, are descriptive (`domain-profile.md` §4, §6).
- Throughput or latency at the declared scale. Scale is data context (`domain-profile.md` §7); the harness does not apply fleet-scale load during functional gates.
=== END OF LISTS ===

You receive the contract: a list of items, each with an id and a requirement.

For each reference requirement, decide how the contract as a whole covers it:

- covered: the items, together, state every obligation of the requirement — every rule, condition, exception, value and outcome it gives. Wording, order, the words chosen for states and roles, and whether a value is given by its name or by its number do not matter; meaning does.
- partial: the items state at least one of its obligations and leave out at least one other.
- missing: no item states any of its obligations.

An item states an obligation only when it says what the service must do, or must not do, in a case the requirement covers. A general wish, such as that the service be reliable, states none. An item that says the opposite of an obligation does not state it. A requirement that only names another one, or a value another one defines, does not take over that other requirement's obligations.

For each item of the contract, decide its class:

- reference: it states one or more obligations of the reference requirements; name each requirement it states obligations of.
- user_visible: it asks for something on the out-of-scope list.
- technical: it asks for something on the list of technical additions.
- other: none of these — it asks for something no reference requirement asks for, or states nothing checkable.

A contract with no items covers nothing.

Reply with JSON only: an object with two keys. "requirements" is a list with exactly one entry for every reference requirement, in the reference's order; each entry has "id", the requirement's id, "coverage", one of "covered", "partial" or "missing", and "items", the ids of the items that state its obligations (an empty list when it is missing). "items" is a list with exactly one entry for every item of the contract, in the contract's order; each entry has "id", the item's id, "class", one of "reference", "user_visible", "technical" or "other", and "requirements", the ids of the reference requirements it states obligations of (an empty list unless its class is "reference").
